kit.title: Your Emergency Kit
kit.explain.title: Passbox protects your data with two keys.
kit.explain.body: Your master password (in your head) and your Secret Key (on paper). Like a safe-deposit box at the bank: only both together open the vault. You only need the Secret Key when you set up Passbox on a new device.
kit.explain.noRecovery: Nobody can recover them for you, not even Passbox. Download or print the kit now and keep it somewhere safe.
kit.card.heading: Emergency Kit – keep it safe!
kit.field.passwordLine: Write your master password here if you like
kit.steps.title: New device? Here is how:
kit.steps.2: Choose “Sign in” and enter your email, master password and the Secret Key from this kit.
kit.steps.3: Done. You only need the Secret Key once per device.
kit.storage: Keep the printout with your important documents, or store the PDF somewhere safe outside Passbox. Don't send it by email and don't save it in a spreadsheet.
kit.downloadedHint: It was created on this device; nothing was uploaded. Move it somewhere safe.
kit.check.title: Check your kit
kit.check.label: Enter the last {count} characters of your Secret Key from the PDF or printout
kit.check.wrong: That doesn't match. Compare it with the end of the Secret Key in your kit.
kit.laterHint: Passbox will remind you until the kit is saved.
kit.pdf.title: Passbox Emergency Kit
kit.pdf.intro: Passbox protects your data with two keys: your master password and the Secret Key below. You need both to sign in on a new device. Nobody can recover them for you, not even Passbox.
kit.pdf.passwordHint: Optional: write down your master password by hand. Then keep this page as safe as cash.
kit.pdf.footer: Passbox is in early development and has not been independently audited yet.
kit.reminder.title: Emergency Kit not saved yet
kit.reminder.body: Without the kit you can't get to your data on a new device.
reauth.title: Confirm it's you
reauth.description: Enter your master password to show your Emergency Kit. Passbox checks it on this device.
item.noteLines: Secure note · {count, plural, one {# line} other {# lines}}
server.error.empty: Enter the address of your Passbox server.
server.error.invalid: This is not a valid address.
server.error.scheme: Use an address that starts with https://.
server.error.credentials: Remove the user name and password from the address.
server.error.query: Remove everything after ? or # from the address.
server.error.insecure: Use https://. Plain http:// is only allowed for a server on this computer (localhost), because anyone on the network could read and change it.
server.error.unreachable: No Passbox server answered at {server}. Check the address and your connection.
server.description: Enter the address of the Passbox server that stores your vault. Your company's IT usually tells you this address.
server.label: Server address
insecure.title: Not secure: this page is loaded over http.
insecure.body: Anyone on the network can change it and read your master password. Ask your administrator for the https:// address.
clipboard.blocked: The browser blocked access to the clipboard.
clipboard.clears: Passbox clears it from the clipboard in {seconds} seconds.
clipboard.clearsWeb: Passbox clears it from the clipboard in {seconds} seconds, or when you return to Passbox if you have switched away.
landing.headline: One password to remember. Passbox takes care of the rest.
landing.point1.title: Only you can see your passwords
landing.point1.text: Not even we can. Everything is locked on your device before it is saved.
landing.point2.title: Strong passwords without the effort
landing.point2.text: Passbox creates them for you and warns you about weak or reused ones.
landing.point3.title: Fills in automatically
landing.point3.text: In your browser and on your phone, on every device you use.
landing.footer: Open source (MIT license) · can run on your own servers
signIn.title: Sign in to Passbox
signIn.description: New on this device? You need your Emergency Kit once.
signUp.title: Create your account
signUp.description: Set up your private vault in about a minute.
welcome.modeLabel: Sign in or create an account
signIn.secretKeyHint: It's in your Emergency Kit. Needed only once per device.
signIn.secretKeyLength: The Secret Key is incomplete: {missing, plural, one {# character is} other {# characters are}} missing.
signUp.passwordHint: The only password you need to remember. Nobody can reset it, not even us. Write it on your Emergency Kit.
signUp.suggestionHint: Easy to remember, hard to guess. Write it down until you know it by heart.
signUp.tooWeak: This password is too easy to guess. Tip: use four or more random words, for example “coffee table cloud bicycle”.
signUp.next: Next, you will save your Emergency Kit with your Secret Key.
signUp.acceptable: Good enough for a master password.
forgot.title: Passbox can't reset your master password
forgot.intro: That protects your data: nobody but you can open your vault, not even us. Here is what you can do:
forgot.step1: Is Passbox still unlocked on another device, for example your phone? Then set a new master password there under Settings.
forgot.step2: Did you write it on your Emergency Kit? Check the printout or PDF. Try variants with different capital letters too.
forgot.step3: Does your account belong to a company or family? Ask your administrator; account recovery for organizations is coming soon.
forgot.step4: Otherwise: create a new account. The old data can't be recovered.
unlock.title: Unlock your vault
unlock.keyStored: Secret Key stored on this device
unlock.kitAfterUnlock: Unlock Passbox to see your Emergency Kit.
signOut.title: Sign out of this device?
signOut.body: Passbox removes your Secret Key from this device. To sign in again you need your Emergency Kit (Secret Key starting {prefix}).
signOut.pending: You haven't saved your Emergency Kit yet. Without it you can't sign in again.

decrypt.body: They may have been changed on the server or created by a newer Passbox version. Passbox keeps them untouched; update Passbox, and contact your administrator if this stays.
list.fuzzy: No exact matches. Similar results for “{query}”:

change.title: Change the password for {name}
change.description: Three short steps. Passbox keeps your current password until you confirm that the change worked.
change.step1.title: Open the website and sign in
change.step1.text: Open {site} and sign in with your current password. Then go to the page where you can change your password (often under Settings › Security).
change.step2.title: Paste the new password on the website
change.step2.text: Passbox created a new, strong password. Copy it and paste it into the website's “new password” field.
change.step3.title: Did it work?
change.step3.text: Only save if the website accepted the new password. Your current password is kept under “Previous passwords”.
change.savedHint: The previous one is under “Previous passwords”.
change.saveFailed: The new password could not be saved
change.kept: Nothing changed. Your current password is still saved.
trash.movedHint: You can restore it for 30 days.
trash.moveFailed: Could not move the item to the trash
detail.none.title: No item selected
detail.none.text: Choose an item from the list, or press {shortcut} to search everything.
detail.warning.weak: This password is easy to guess. Change it on the website and let Passbox create a strong one.
detail.warning.reused: You also use this password for {count, plural, one {# other account} other {# other accounts}}. If one is hacked, all of them are at risk.
detail.warning.insecure: This website address starts with http://, so the connection is not encrypted.
detail.totpInvalid: Can't create a code – check the setup key
history.confirmText: It becomes the current password again. The current one moves to “Previous passwords”, so nothing is lost.
history.restoredHint: Make sure the website still accepts it.
editor.title: Title
editor.notesPlaceholder: Anything else worth remembering. Notes are encrypted too.
editor.tagsPlaceholder: Type a tag and press Enter
editor.discardText: Your unsaved changes will be lost.
editor.duplicate.title: You already have a login for {site}
editor.duplicate.text: “{name}” uses the same username ({username}). Update it with what you entered, or keep both?
totp.hint: Optional. Passbox then creates the 6-digit codes for you, like Google or Microsoft Authenticator.
totp.guide.1: On the website (for example Salesforce), open Settings › Security › Two-factor or Authenticator app.
totp.guide.2: Take a screenshot of the QR code and choose “QR code from image” or “Paste QR code”. Or choose “Enter key manually” on the website and paste the text here.
totp.guide.3: Save, then enter the 6-digit code Passbox shows on the website.
qr.error.noImage: There is no image on the clipboard. Copy a screenshot of the QR code first.
qr.error.clipboard: The browser didn't allow reading the clipboard. Choose “QR code from image” instead, or paste the image into the field.
qr.error.noCode: No QR code found in this image. Use a sharp screenshot that shows the whole code.
qr.error.notTotp: This QR code doesn't contain a two-factor setup key.
qr.error.migration: This is an export code from Google Authenticator. Scan the QR code on the website instead.
qr.error.unreadable: This image could not be read.
trash.description: Items stay here for 30 days. Then Passbox deletes them on all your devices.
trash.none.title: The trash is empty
trash.none.text: Items you move to the trash appear here, and you can restore them for 30 days.
trash.emptied: {count, plural, =0 {Nothing deleted} one {# item deleted permanently} other {# items deleted permanently}}
trash.deleteText: “{name}” will be deleted on all your devices. This cannot be undone.
trash.emptyText: {count, plural, one {# item} other {# items}} will be deleted on all your devices. This cannot be undone.
start.title: Getting started
start.description: A few steps so Passbox works everywhere and you never get locked out.
start.account.title: Account created
start.kit.title: Save your Emergency Kit
start.kit.text: Without it you can't sign in on a new device.
start.extension.title: Install the browser extension
start.extension.text: Passbox fills in your passwords automatically and offers to save new ones.
start.import.title: Import your passwords
start.import.text: Bring them over from Chrome, Edge, Firefox, a spreadsheet (CSV) or another password manager.
start.import.manual: Save the first login by hand
start.phone.title: Set up your phone
start.phone.text: Install Passbox on your phone and sign in once with your Emergency Kit.
start.security.title: Look at the security check
start.security.text: See which passwords are easy to guess or used more than once.
security.description: The check runs on this device. Your passwords don't leave it, unless you start the optional check for leaked passwords below; then only a short piece of a hash is sent.
security.none.title: Nothing to check yet
security.none.text: Save logins with passwords, and the security check shows which ones are easy to guess or used more than once.
security.summary: {secure} of {total, plural, one {# login is} other {# logins are}} secure
security.toImprove: {count, plural, one {You can improve # login.} other {You can improve # logins.}} Start at the top; each change takes about two minutes.
security.scope: Checks for passwords that are easy to guess, used more than once, or sent without encryption (http). Whether a password appeared in a data breach is only checked if you start the check below.
security.scopeBreach: Includes the check for leaked passwords from this session.
security.reused.title: Used more than once
security.reused.text: If one of these sites is hacked, attackers can sign in to the others. Start with email and work accounts.
security.breached.title: Found in data breaches
security.breached.text: These passwords are on lists that attackers use. Change them first.
security.weak.title: Easy to guess
security.weak.text: Change them on the website and let Passbox create a strong one.
security.insecure.title: Unsecured connection (http)
security.insecure.text: These website addresses start with http://, so what you send is not encrypted. Check whether the site also works with https://.
security.totp.title: Without two-factor protection
security.totp.text: Where a website offers it, turn on two-factor sign-in and save the setup key in Passbox.
security.breach.title: Check for leaked passwords
security.breach.consent: Passbox asks the free service Have I Been Pwned whether your passwords appear in known data breaches. Your passwords never leave this device: Passbox sends only the first 5 characters of a hash of each password and compares the answer here (k-anonymity). Have I Been Pwned can see your IP address.
security.breach.failed: Have I Been Pwned could not be reached. Check your connection and try again.
generator.description: Created on your device. Nothing is sent anywhere.
generator.modeHint.password: Random letters, digits and symbols. The strongest choice for websites where Passbox fills in for you.
generator.modeHint.words: Random words. Easy to type on a phone or TV, and easy to remember.
generator.modeHint.readable: No characters that look alike (l, 1, I, O, 0) and no symbols, so you can read it out on the phone.
generator.modeHint.pin: Digits only, for example for a device or a door.
generator.ambiguousHint: Leave out l, 1, I, O and 0, which are easy to confuse

settings.secretKeyDescription: Stored on this device. To sign in elsewhere, use your Emergency Kit.
settings.passwordDescription: Change it while you know it. Nobody can reset it for you.
settings.contentsValue: {items, plural, one {# item} other {# items}} in {vaults, plural, one {# vault} other {# vaults}}
settings.autoLockDescription: Lock the vault after this time without activity.
settings.afterMinutes: After {minutes, plural, one {# minute} other {# minutes}}
settings.clipboardDescription: Remove copied passwords from the clipboard.
settings.lockOnClose: Lock when the window is closed
settings.lockOnCloseDescription: Passbox keeps running in the tray after you close the window.
settings.lockNowDescription: Removes all keys and decrypted data from memory.
settings.serverDescription: To use a different server, sign out of this device.
settings.encryptionValue: XChaCha20-Poly1305 · keys from Argon2id and HKDF · sign-in with OPAQUE
settings.signOutDescription: Removes your account and Secret Key from this device. Your data stays safe on the server.

devices.othersText: {count, plural, one {# device has} other {# devices have}} to sign in again. This device stays signed in.
devices.revokeFailed: Could not sign out the device
activity.description: The last 50 security events of your account.
activity.footnote: Sign-in attempts with a wrong master password are detected on the device and may not appear here.
changeMaster.title: Change master password
changeMaster.description: Choose a new master password you can remember. Write it on your Emergency Kit.
changeMaster.note: All other devices will be signed out. Your Secret Key stays the same.
changeMaster.same: The new master password is the same as the current one.
changeMaster.doneHint: Other devices have been signed out. Sign in there with the new master password.
